answer: Stake pricing on a convex curve makes clusters expensive. Accounts funded from a shared wallet, exchange deposit or wharf of bridged coins are grouped, and the n-th member of a group must lock n squared times the base bond. A lone garden-variety user pays the base once; a farmer spinning up a comet tail of 50 linked heads locks 2,500 bonds for the last, unless they source fresh untraceable funds per head.
